pr_title: fix(optimizer): alias dep entrypoints for yarn pnp compat (Fixes #1748)
pr_body:
Fixes #1748
Since esbuild is not providing any way to customize out destination, the workaround is to alias entrypoints using plugin callbacks
pr_comments: A similar strategy is used in 04f9dc6

issue_context.title: [yarn pnp] Dep optimizer does not work with virtual path (peer-dependencies)
issue_context.body: **⚠️ IMPORTANT ⚠️ Please check the following list before proceeding. If you ignore this issue template, your issue will be directly closed.** - [x] Read [the docs](https://vitejs.dev/guide/). - [x] Use Vite >=2.0. (1.x is no longer supported) - [x] If the issue is related to 1.x -> 2.0 upgrade, read the [Migration Guide](https://vitejs.dev/guide/migration.html) first. ## Describe the bug When using peer dependencies Yarn is creating virtual paths, when vite optimize deps it keeps the file structure: Now yarn here is modifying the behaviour of native existsSync and return false despite the folder exists in the cache. This condition fails and does not preprend the FS_PREFIX to the path resulting in a 404 https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/2950c3c278e20174184e44c194393b098c0d4305/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/importAnalysis.ts#L184 Sorry for submitting another issue related to yarn2, I understand that moving forward you don't want to invest more energy in supporting it. We are considering other solutions Maybe @merceyz or @arcanis can chime in here ? ## Reproduction https://github.com/AlexandreBonaventure/vite-yarn-optimize-virtual ## System Info - `vite` version: 2.0.0-beta.50 - Operating System: Mac OS - Node version: 14 - Package manager (npm/yarn/pnpm) and version: yarn 2
comments:
This is because since the filesystem structure is preserved (including the `$$virtual/hash/<n>` part), the virtual component gets interpreted by the virtual filesystem layer (ie the one that makes `/foo/$$virtual/hash/0/hello` equal to `/foo/hello`).

I'm not sure what would be the right fix here - an easy one would be to simply "escape" the `$$virtual` part into something else (for example by turning it into `yarn-virtual`), but it means adding a bit of code for to help for Yarn compat.

Vite should probably only preserve the part of the path after `node_modules/`, I don't think it's supposed to keep everything after `<cwd>/`

> Sorry for submitting another issue related to yarn2, I understand that moving forward you don't want to invest more energy in supporting it. We are considering other solutions

Again, Yarn 2 !== Yarn PnP, just like Yarn 1, Yarn 2 supports both PnP and node_modules
The pre-bundled dep file paths are generated by esbuild. There's currently no way to customize output paths in esbuild so this is a wontfix unless esbuild allows such customizations.
yup I did some research, but fun timing I've just found a workaround

I think your fix is not a working right cause its not create a sub folder inside `node_modules/.vite/` and throw an error, if the entry points file names are the same like `index.js`. For testing purpose you can add two dependencies `react` and `react-dom` and import them in the main file. The proper way would be if its generate a submodule for each entry points like `node_modules/.vite/react/index.js`.

```
(this will be run only when your dependencies or config have changed)
 > error: Two output files share the same path but have different contents: node_modules/.vite/index.js.map

 > error: Two output files share the same path but have different contents: node_modules/.vite/index.js
```
The fix currently won't work because the proxy entries need to preserve the signature of the original entry instead of just importing it.

yes, the PR has some flaws (https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/1748#issuecomment-769242098). I'll try to see if we can make it work somehow... 
However it seemingly preserved the signature from what I can see in my repro. To be honest I did not spend much time on this.
The PR does help because esbuild's output path behavior has been a source of bugs. I think I can refactor it to generate the file structure that I want with the technique used in your PR...
Can confirm this is fixed as of 32ba8fb
